topic.angle: Why 1900 was not a leap year

body.question: Was 1900 a leap year?
body.reveal: No. A leap day every 4 years is slightly too much, because the year is about 365.2422 days, not 365.25. That adds up to about 3 extra days every 400 years. So years divisible by 100 skip the leap day unless they are also divisible by 400: 2000 was a leap year, 1900 was not.

probes.question: Years divisible by 100 are leap years only if they are also divisible by ____.
True or false: 2100 will be a leap year.

claims.claim: Leap-year rule: every 4 years except years divisible by 100 but not by 400 (cloze 400; reveal)
claims.quote: this extra leap day occurs in each year that is a multiple of 4, except for years evenly divisible by 100 but not by 400.

claims.claim: 2000 was a leap year, 1900 was not, 2100 will not be (probe 2 false)
claims.quote: Thus 1600, 2000 and 2400 are leap years, but 1700, 1800, 1900, 2100, 2200, and 2300 are not.

claims.claim: A year is about 365.2422 days, not 365.25
claims.quote: a Julian year lasts 365.25 days, a mean tropical year about 365.2422 days

claims.claim: A leap day every 4 years drifts about 3 days every 400 years
claims.quote: Consequently, even this Julian calendar drifts out of 'true' by about 3 days every 400 years.
